data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains rather than describes when the guard's declared data model and the subject's added behavior diverge \u2014 the 3-of-26 survivors are one bug in two costumes: guards that check declared data cannot see added behavior, and the installation ritual only makes this divergence load-bearing.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If at least one survivor alters declared data and still escapes, the declared-data/added-behavior distinction is not exhaustive.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the compile.py 1/9 loss involves a guard that checks behavior rather than data, then the mechanism is not uniform across the repository.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If a behavior-guard mutation would be caught even under installation, then the constraint is not on data declaration.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the author's care is uniformly distributed, the spread should be narrower than observed.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The record's own finding ('THE THREE SURVIVORS ARE ONE BUG IN TWO COSTUMES: a guard that checks DECLARED DATA does not see ADDED BEHAVIOUR') suggests the test is an enforcement of a data schema, not a description of runtime behavior. Under shown-to-fail-first installation, the subject is normalized to match the declared data before testing, so mutations that only alter behavior are invisible. The 4/4 to 6/7 spread across ordinarily-guarded modules is the variance in how much added behavior each module carries relative to its declared surface.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
